title: Wisdom of Crowds: Cross-sectional Variation in the Informativeness of Third-Party-Generated Product Information on Twitter

scopes.description: Complete author-documented workflow: manual SPSS GUI data preparation, local/vendor data acquisition and two supplied SPSS table-analysis syntax files.

requirements.description: Compustat quarterly company data required to form quarterly revenue/sales growth, other quarterly controls and q−4 lagged values. The documented extract starts 2010-01-01 and was downloaded 2016-12-30; each included outcome needs the four-quarter source observation, with the earliest needed date unresolved because the analysis start is not stated. The exact Compustat sales/revenue field and ticker-to-author OFFICIAL TICKER mapping need confirmation.

routes.description: Readable local COMP.FUNDQ candidate with quarterly dates, fiscal year/quarter, SALEQ and REVTQ. Local access and columns are verified; required source-period coverage and which sales-versus-revenue field the author uses are not. The existing local resource is a candidate; the one-row probe is not treated as a reason to reconfirm a license or exact author download vintage.
routes.expected_period: Author filter: 2010-01-01 through download date 2016-12-30; require q−4 history before each included outcome, exact earliest needed date unresolved.

requirements.description: Compustat annual company name, GVKEY, fiscal year, annual sales and annual advertising expense are required to build lagged annual sales/advertising and prorated quarterly advertising. The author starts 2010-01-01 and downloads through 2016-12-31; the prior-fiscal-year lag requires history before each included row, exact earliest needed date unresolved.

routes.description: Readable local COMP.FUNDA candidate with GVKEY, DATADATE, FYEAR, SALE, REVT, XAD, TIC, CONM. Local access and columns are verified; required annual history and the author field mapping are not. The existing local resource is a candidate; the one-row probe is not treated as a reason to reconfirm a license or exact author download vintage.
routes.expected_period: Author filter: 2010-01-01 through download date 2016-12-31; retain preceding fiscal-year history for the lag, exact earliest needed date unresolved.

requirements.description: I/B/E/S Summary Tape quarterly sales analyst forecasts and realized sales are required to create LASTFORECAST.SAV and unexpected sales growth. The author uses data downloaded 2016-12-09, selects the last calendar-time forecast for each official ticker/fiscal period end using STATPER, and removes 83 rows without realized sales. The start date, sales MEASURE/value, currency, realized-sales mapping and local STATPERS versus documented STATPER field naming are unresolved.

routes.description: Readable local IBES.STATSUM_XEPSUS summary-history candidate contains OFTIC, STATPERS, FPEDATS, MEASURE, FISCALP, FPI, MEANEST and ACTUAL. Local access and columns are verified; which MEASURE denotes quarterly sales, whether ACTUAL is realized sales for that measure, history coverage, and author STATPER/local STATPERS field naming remain unresolved. No exact author-era download vintage is required absent a documented vintage dependency.
routes.expected_period: Quarterly sales forecast history through 2016-12-09; author start date not specified; period range must cover matched Compustat quarters.

routes.description: Readable local unadjusted summary-history candidate has estimate, ticker and period fields but no ACTUAL column; it does not satisfy the realized-sales requirement on its own. It is a partial catalog candidate, not a claim that a new author-specific purchase is required.
routes.expected_period: Quarterly sales forecast history through 2016-12-09; start not specified.

requirements.description: LikeFolio company-day product information is a mandatory full-pipeline source for 2012-01-01–2015-12-31: DATE, TICKER and the vendor’s per-million PRODUCTTWEET, PURCHASETWEET, POSITIVETWEET and NEGATIVETWEET statistics, built using proprietary tweet-holder/target, purchase and valence classifications and product-to-company mapping. The author uses PURCHASETWEET directly and constructs POSITIVE from the positive and negative fields. The documented moving-average window is 91 days before each quarterly endpoint; whether retained earliest endpoints need pre-2012 history depends on the author’s initial-window and sample handling, which is not specified. Do not widen the stated 2012–2015 source period without evidence. Author redistribution terms do not establish whether a separate replicator license exists.

routes.description: The official LikeFolio homepage currently describes API/bulk delivery and daily consumer trends with stated history from 2016. It does not verify the author’s 2012–2015 per-million company-day product, its four fields/classification contract, or an authorized route for this replicator. The author agreement prevents assuming the author can redistribute their copy; separate access remains unknown.
routes.expected_period: Author vendor series: 2012-01-01 through 2015-12-31. The documented 91-day moving average requires checking retained first endpoint handling; additional pre-2012 dates are conditional on those endpoints and the author’s rule, not presumed.

requirements.description: Additional LikeFolio tweet-handle classification statistics are required for the B2C subsample and tables 7–9. The source is company-month data delivered to the author on 2017-03-10, classified as media, product experts and crowd, supporting category shares of product tweets plus category PURCHASE and POSITIVE statistics. The analysis computes three-month monthly moving averages from two months before through the current month. Exact source columns, units, class construction and monthly date range are not specified. The two-month rolling history requirement for the earliest retained month depends on the author’s initial-window and sample handling.

routes.location: LikeFolio direct access to monthly B2C tweet-handle classifications
routes.description: The author reports additional vendor data but the package includes neither raw monthly classifications nor a compatible prepared SAV. Current provider pages do not document these monthly handle categories or fields. A separate authorized route, population, schema, and date coverage remain unverified; no classification reconstruction is supported.
routes.expected_period: Company-month B2C subset; supplied to author on 2017-03-10; date range not stated; three-month moving average from t−2 through t. Verify initial-window history based on the first retained month and the author’s handling.

software.name: IBM SPSS Statistics 24
software.description: The author requires IBM SPSS Statistics Version 24. Both supplied native SPSS syntax files use GENLIN with /REPEATED for GEE, normal identity models and robust covariance. IBM v24 documentation confirms that GENLIN with REPEATED fits GEE; current IBM documentation lists Standard Edition or Advanced Statistics for GENLIN. A bounded PATH lookup found no spss/statistics/pspp command, but desktop installation, v24 compatibility and applicable module/license entitlement are unverified.

issues.description: The 12-stage raw-to-analysis preparation workflow is documented as SPSS GUI/menu steps, not supplied executable preparation syntax. It remains part of the full pipeline and must be carried out manually once compatible inputs and SPSS access are available; the two .sps files are output analysis programs only.

Each supplied analysis file starts with SAVE OUTFILE to copy the currently active SPSS dataset and then applies filters; neither opens a named input with GET FILE. The correct author-prepared SAV must be open/active before the corresponding syntax runs, with model variables and INTABLE flags present. The datasheet once says IBES_TWITTR.SAV, whereas Step 12 and the native syntax use IBES_TWITTER.SAV; confirm the intended prepared file name.

Both native SPSS files write first to an absolute [redacted-path-dc0585283f88]... path. The destination is author-machine specific and must be configured to an accessible writable folder for the eventual runtime; no replacement path is assumed.

The readable local Compustat and I/B/E/S candidates show relevant columns, but the author’s exact quarterly sales-versus-revenue field, ticker mapping, I/B/E/S sales MEASURE and actual field, STATPER/STATPERS field naming, and complete required history are not established. Quarterly q−4 and annual one-year lag history must be retained; exact earliest required dates cannot be inferred from the broad 2010 filter alone. No identical 2016 download vintage is required absent a documented vintage dependency.

The LikeFolio requirement is the author’s 2012–2015 per-million company-day series. The current official provider page describes a current daily product with stated history from 2016 but does not verify this same historical series, its fields/classification contract, or an independent access route. For the documented 91-day moving average, first-window history depends on the actual retained endpoints and author handling; additional pre-2012 data are not presumed. This does not establish lack of a license or justify rebuilding proprietary classifications.

The monthly vendor documentation names media/expert/crowd measures (including printed labels MEIDA_AVG_PURCHASE and CROWD_AVG_PURCAHSE), while the analysis syntax expects ln_avg_news_purchase plus corrected news/expert/crowd positive variables. Exact raw columns, category denominator/units, media-to-news mapping, typos, and corrected-positive construction are unsupported. The two-month rolling history for the first retained month depends on author initial-window and sample handling; do not guess aliases or reconstruct the proprietary classification.

The analysis syntax requires INTABLE5, INTABLE6 and INTABLE789 flags, but their producers and membership rules are not present in the supplied syntax. The datasheet describes a B2C subset by major customer base and the Excel files list GVKEYs; neither supplies full analysis rows or the flag construction. Obtain exact B2C, table-sample and GVKEY membership definitions before treating the filtered SAVs as ready.

evidence.description: Compustat quarterly source filter starts 2010-01-01 and was downloaded 2016-12-30; negative revenue observations are deleted.

The documented daily Likefolio fields are PRODUCTTWEET, PURCHASETWEET, POSITIVETWEET, and NEGATIVETWEET, each per-million normalized.
Author says the vendor agreement does not permit the author to share extracted Twitter information or collection/calculation methods.
Author defines daily PURCHASE from PURCHASETWEET and POSITIVE as POSITIVETWEET divided by positive plus negative; intermediate is TWITTER_RAW.SAV.
Company-quarter AVG_PURCHASE and AVG_POSITIVE use moving averages over the 91 days before and including each date.

Table 7–9 syntax begins by saving the already-active dataset to an author-machine absolute path; it does not initialize an input with GET FILE.

Table 7–9 analysis uses GENLIN with normal identity and repeated NAICS groups, independent working correlation, robust covariance.

Check the existing COMP.FUNDA candidate for the documented annual-sales and XAD advertising variables and the author’s 2010-01-01–2016-12-31 period; retain a prior-fiscal-year row only where required by the annual lag.

Use IBES.STATSUM_XEPSUS as the primary local candidate and identify the MEASURE value that denotes quarterly sales, whether ACTUAL is the matching realized-sales value, and the STATPERS/STATPER naming relationship. Use the author’s 2016-12-09 cutoff and last-forecast selection by official ticker and fiscal-period end. The unadjusted local alternative lacks ACTUAL and is not sufficient alone.

If the exact source-field value or alias cannot be established from the current data documentation, request only that specific mapping. The documented dates are source bounds/cutoffs; an identical author-era file vintage is not a prerequisite absent evidence of a vintage-dependent construction.

actions.description: Follow the author’s documented SPSS GUI preparation sequence for all tables; the two supplied .sps files do not replace this manual stage.
steps: With compatible sources available, prepare the quarterly I/B/E/S sales forecast input and create LASTFORECAST.SAV using the stated ticker/period key, last-forecast selection and realized-sales missing-value rule.

Prepare quarterly and annual Compustat inputs; apply documented filters, duplicate handling and q−4/annual lags; prorate quarterly advertising; merge to create COMPALL.SAV, then merge with LASTFORECAST.SAV to create COMP_IBES.SAV.

As a separate input branch, prepare the documented monthly B2C handle-classification averages in TWITTERAVG_HANDLE.SAV. Create COMP_TWITTER.SAV from ALL.SAV for tables 5–6; then join the B2C subset to TWITTERAVG_HANDLE.SAV by ticker and MONTHINDEX, apply the documented rank/missing-value/outlier steps, and create IBES_TWITTER.SAV for tables 7–9.
Keep the required output order and intermediate SAV files. The Excel GVKEY workbooks are identification lists only and cannot stand in for any of these generated analysis datasets.

review_notes: Expanded source/evidence checkpoint saved after manual review of all 300 datasheet lines and both complete SPSS syntax files. Local catalog/probe/public-page checks are bounded; no author code was executed. Requirements, issues and actions are being added incrementally.

Prior evidence-update construction attempt failed with SyntaxError: unterminated string literal (detected at line 66); the prior draft checkpoint was retained and the error was logged in draft_build_errors.json.

Five mandatory data requirements are now checkpointed: Compustat quarterly, Compustat annual, I/B/E/S quarterly sales forecasts/actuals, LikeFolio company-day product stats, and separate monthly tweet-handle classification data. All available routes remain unverified for specific product/field/history compatibility; no redistribution or license absence is inferred.

Software and issue checkpoint saved. Manual GUI preparation is credited separately from the two substantive analysis syntax files; runtime/license and GENLIN edition remain unverified. Issues distinguish documented preparation from unresolved source history, handle-variable mapping and table-sample flags.

Calibration update: retained the local readable Compustat/I/B/E/S candidates without adding a blanket license or exact author-vintage prerequisite. The 91-day daily and two-month monthly rolling histories are conditional on actual retained endpoints and author initial-window handling; no pre-2012 extension is presumed.

The frozen work item contains no dependency checklist IDs; the supplied SPSS sources are manually traced. No analysis_only scope is added because the package has only GVKEY lists, not full compatible COMP_TWITTER.SAV/IBES_TWITTER.SAV analysis data, and no supported standalone analysis-input route.

The proposal preserves the separate daily LikeFolio 2012–2015 and monthly B2C handle-classification contracts, keeps rolling-window initial history conditional on retained endpoints/author handling, and leaves all author code unexecuted.
